dimensions.assessment: Affects state child welfare agencies, child protective services workers, and families with children participating in independent activities across states.
dimensions.evidence: State child protective services agencies are burdened by frivolous reports that undermine reasonable childhood independence

dimensions.assessment: Alters state child welfare policies, staff training mandates, and risk assessment protocols to prevent investigations solely due to reasonable independence activities.
dimensions.evidence: prevent unnecessary and traumatic investigations of parents or the separation of a child from a parent... solely due to the child participating in reasonable childhood independence activities

dimensions.assessment: Requires the Department of Health and Human Services to conduct a study and report, but does not specify direct funding authorizations for grants.
dimensions.evidence: the Secretary of Health and Human Services shall conduct a study

dimensions.assessment: Modifies the Social Security Act and the Child Abuse Prevention and Treatment Act by adding new state plan requirements, definitions, and training mandates.
dimensions.evidence: To amend subpart 2 of part B of title IV of the Social Security Act... to amend the Child Abuse Prevention and Treatment Act

dimensions.assessment: Imposes permanent statutory changes on federal-state child welfare program requirements and grant eligibility conditions.
dimensions.evidence: The amendments made by this Act shall take effect on the 1st day of the 1st fiscal year beginning on or after the date of the enactment

missing_information: Specific cost estimates or appropriation amounts for carrying out the required study and grant condition changes.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill mandates a federal study, alters state plan requirements under Title IV of the Social Security Act, and amends the Child Abuse Prevention and Treatment Act to address child welfare investigations related to childhood independence activities.
